Priyanka D: Noticed two OOM exits on kv-shard-31 during today's canary ramp (14:10). Process logged "runtime: out of memory". Uploading pprofs to s3://redwood/debug/kv/4999990001.tgz
Marco V: Can you drop the pprof top or a short heap summary? We need to know if this is live-set growth or fragmentation.
Priyanka D: quick top (alloc_space):
```
pprof: top
48MB  runtime.mallocgc
27MB  github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Shard).applyBatch
11MB  github.com/redwood/runtime/cache.newEntry
```
Ivy Z: That applyBatch ramp looks similar to last month's incidents after bulk enrich. Immediate mitigation: enable a shard-level soft-cap (70%) and set ephemeral eviction TTL=45s on the canary subset. I can flip and monitor.
Harold F: I'll own profiling automation: capture heap at t0/t+5/t+25, run `go tool pprof -inuse_space -alloc_space`, and produce a symbol-diff. Will post script to INF-5233. ETA tomorrow morning.
ops-bot: Created INF-5233: "kv-shard-31 OOM triage" (assigned: Harold F) :white_check_mark:
Marco V: Long-term signal ask: add a "contiguous_free_ratio" per shard and a moving-window live_object_count. That should help distinguish fragmentation vs live growth in charting. Owner suggestion: Ivy for schema, Marco for Console wiring.
Ivy Z: I can prototype an exporter that emits slab_contiguous_free and slab_total; will try a simple histogram and push to Prom. Target: demo in next sprint.
Priyanka D: Action list (adding to postmortem follow-ups):
- A1: Apply and validate soft-cap + ephemeral eviction on kv-shard-31 (owner: Ivy Z) — due: 2026-03-31
- A2: Heap diff automation + symbol diff (owner: Harold F) — due: 2026-03-30
- A3: GC early-run experiment (tune GOGC 100->200) to check fragmentation sensitivity (owner: Marco V) — due: 2026-04-02
- A4: Frag metric exporter + dashboard mock (owners: Ivy Z / Marco V) — due: 2026-04-09
- A5: Postmortem follow-up check-in (owner: Priyanka D) — due: 2026-04-12
Marco V: I'll also add a short recurring-pattern check in the postmortem doc: if we see the applyBatch spike within 30m after bulk writes 3x in 30 days, mark as recurring and trigger RFC for allocator/compaction.
Harold F: After I finish the diff script I'll upload tarball and link INF-5233. If diffs show many small retained slices, we should consider a slab coalescing R&D ticket.
Ivy Z: Soft-cap rolled to canary at 14:25; initial evict_count=73 in 20m, p99 latency impact minimal. No new OOMs in canary so far.
Priyanka D: Thanks everyone. Please keep updates in INF-5233; we'll surface the consolidated timeline in next retro and mark recurring-pattern if tests reproduce. :thumbsup:
